title: Miketz: it is not in me (Genesis 41:16)
hookLine: Joseph tells Pharaoh the meaning comes from God, not from him

cards: You finally get the meeting with the big boss. Or the audition, or the chance to pitch the idea to the person who can make it happen. And they say: I hear you're the one who can do this.
The easy reply is: yes, that's me. Joseph has just been pulled out of the dungeon, shaved and changed. He's standing in Pharaoh's court, a prisoner one hour ago.
Pharaoh says: I've had a dream, and I've heard that you can read dreams.

teach.b: Joseph's first words to Pharaoh, in the old Jewish Publication Society translation: "It is not in me; God will give Pharaoh an answer of peace." In Hebrew, the first part is a single word, biladai. Not me.
Apart from me. Think about the risk. Joseph needs Pharaoh to think he's valuable; he has one shot to get out of prison for good.
And the first thing he does is hand the credit away. Remember the young Joseph, seventeen, telling his brothers about dreams where their sheaves bowed down to his?

teach.h: THE BOY WHO TALKED ABOUT HIMSELF.
teach.b: That Joseph talked a lot about himself. This one, after the pit and the prison, talks about God. And he keeps doing it.
Pharaoh tells both dreams, the cows and the ears of grain, and Joseph says: God has told Pharaoh what he is about to do. Seven years of plenty, seven years of famine.
The dream came twice because the thing is fixed by God, and God will do it soon. Again and again, Joseph names God. Here's the surprise: giving the credit away doesn't make him smaller.
Pharaoh looks around his court and asks: could we find anyone like this, a man with the spirit of God in him? And he puts Joseph over all of Egypt. The rabbis prized this.

teach.h: SAY IT IN THE NAME OF WHO SAID IT.
teach.b: The Mishnah says that whoever repeats a teaching in the name of the one who said it brings redemption into the world.
The lesson they drew is plain: say where things came from.

how: Jewish learning takes care to cite who said what, and students repeat teachings in the name of the teacher who first taught them, following the Mishnah's saying about bringing redemption.

o: the dreamer, the portion of the burning bush
at the end, the portion where Joseph meets Pharaoh
he rose up, Joseph's climb to power in Egypt

games.q: what's inside the scene — tap the pairs.
p: I've heard you can read dreams
the thing is fixed by God
say it in the name of who said it

s: Joseph told Pharaoh he had a gift for dreams
his first words were: it is not in me; God will give Pharaoh an answer.
giving credit to God made Pharaoh doubt Joseph
Pharaoh asked, could we find anyone like this, with the spirit of God in him?
Joseph named God again and again before Pharaoh
God has told Pharaoh what he is about to do, he says, more than once.

games.q: Pharaoh says: I hear you can read dreams. this is your one chance to leave prison. you're Joseph. what do you say?
o: it is not in me; God will answer.
games.why: Joseph said, it is not in me; God will give Pharaoh an answer of peace. Pharaoh set him over all Egypt.

practice: Think of something you're proud of lately: a good result at work, a meal, a kid who's doing well, a hard day you got through. Trace it back: who taught you, who helped, what was given to you that you didn't make yourself?
If you pray, you can thank God for it; either way, choose one person you could name out loud.

wordCard.voice: Miketz. At the end: the portion where Joseph, before Pharaoh, says the meaning isn't in him, but comes from God.

orig.note: Hebrew: not me, apart from me. Joseph's first word to Pharaoh.

carryVoice: Your line: not in me. In his one big chance, Joseph's first word pointed past himself. See you tomorrow.

sources.q: It is not in me; God will give Pharaoh an answer of peace.
